claim: End-to-end joint training of a physically consistent rigid-body dynamics model, sign-friction component and residual LSTM improves inverse-dynamics prediction and enables more precise joint-space impedance tracking at low feedback gains than the reported two-step hybrid baseline on tested Franka Panda free-space trajectories; it does not establish universal superiority, contact safety, passivity or closed-loop stability.
claim_locator: Model formulation; offline comparisons; motion-tracking experiments and Table III; conclusion.
epistemic_status: robotics method with offline model evaluation and real-robot control experiments
problem_and_setting: Using physical priors plus recurrent residual learning to improve precision under compliant low feedback gains on a 7-DoF Franka Panda.
method_or_mechanism: A fully physically consistent RBD parameterization plus simplified sign friction and residual LSTM is trained end-to-end. LSTM memory models history-dependent friction, flexibility and partial observability. Comparators include two-step hybrid, MLP residual, RBD and black-box LSTM.
content_summary: Offline 10-seed tests generally favor the hybrid over black-box LSTM and RBD, while MLP fits training better and LSTM generalizes better; the last joint is an exception. Online 1000 Hz control uses five minimum-jerk trajectories under soft, medium and stiff gains. E2E hybrid RMSE is 12.799°, 2.244° and 0.744° versus two-step 16.207°, 2.599° and 0.763°. Final offsets are 18.401°, 3.125°, 0.992° versus 24.45°, 2.304°, 0.596°, so E2E does not dominate every metric. Black-box LSTM entered joint-angle constraints and failed.
synthesis_role: Primary evidence for physical-prior plus learned-residual feedforward compensation improving the compliance–precision trade-off, while exposing extrapolation and guarantee gaps.
development_link: Connects inverse-dynamics hybrid learning to low-gain impedance tracking rather than direct impedance adaptation.

evidence.finding: Hybrid LSTM generally outperformed black-box LSTM and RBD; MLP trained better but LSTM generalized better, with a last-joint exception.
E2E hybrid RMSE was 12.799/2.244/0.744° for soft/medium/stiff gains versus two-step 16.207/2.599/0.763°.
E2E offsets were 18.401/3.125/0.992° versus two-step 24.45/2.304/0.596°, so E2E was not best for every metric.
Soft gains were about two orders below stiff gains, making tracking depend strongly on model accuracy.
Black-box LSTM entered joint-angle constraints and its online control evaluation failed.

boundary_conditions: One Franka Panda and related free-space trajectories were used.
No contact-rich, collision or force-safety evaluation exists.
Physical consistency applies to the RBD part, not the full learned loop.
No closed-loop stability or passivity proof exists.
No online confidence intervals or hypothesis tests are reported.
assumptions: Robot-specific identification data represent deployment dynamics.
External torque is absent or negligible.
Recurrent state is initialized over 500 iterations.
Low-gain operation stays within the trained distribution.

reported: E2E did not dominate medium/stiff final offsets.
inferred: Physical consistency does not prove full-loop passivity or stability.
Free-space compliance does not establish contact safety.
Single-robot evaluation leaves distribution shift unresolved.
The black-box failure is not a universal theorem about black-box models.

verification_status: verified against Controller-supplied admitted full-text extraction
